info.title: mailcow REST API v2
info.description:
mailcow REST API v2 runs next to the legacy mailcow UI and `/api/v1`, which keep working
unchanged. It is the only backend of the mailcowui-ng web app. This document is the source of
truth: the implementation mirrors it exactly, and undocumented behaviour is a bug.

## Conventions

- Names are camelCase. Booleans are `true`/`false`. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC.
- A single resource is returned as `{"data": {...}}`. A list is returned as
  `{"data": [...], "meta": {"total", "limit", "offset"}}` and accepts `limit` (default 25, at
  most 1,000), `offset`, `sort`, `order`, a substring search `q` and the documented filters.
- Create returns `201` with a `Location` header, read and update return `200`, delete returns
  `204`. Non-CRUD actions are sub-resources (for example `POST /api-keys/{apiKeyId}/revocation`)
  and return `200` with the affected resource or the ceremony data.
- `PATCH` takes JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396, `application/merge-patch+json`).
- Mutable resources carry a version tag: a strong ETag over their stored settings, never over
  usage data. A single read returns it in the `ETag` header, and every representation,
  including each list entry, carries the same value in `etag`. Writes accept `If-Match` and
  answer `412` when it does not match. The legacy UI edits the same rows, so clients should
  send it.

## Errors

Every error is an RFC 9457 problem (`application/problem+json`) with `type`, `title`,
`status`, `detail` and `requestId`. Problem types that clients act on are relative URI
references of the form `/api/v2/problems/{name}`, documented in `docs/problems.md` and served
as HTML by `GET /problems/{problemType}`. Compare `type` as an exact string. Other problems
use `about:blank` and are identified by their status (`400` malformed request, `404` unknown
resource or path, `405` method not allowed, `409` conflict described in `detail`, `412`
precondition failed, `500` unexpected failure).

Errors are never localised: the API ignores `Accept-Language`. `title` and `detail` are
English and meant for logs and scripts. A validation problem (`422`) carries an `errors` map
from each invalid field to a list of violations, each with a stable rule `code` and its
`params`, so that clients build translated messages themselves.

## Authentication

**Browser clients** use a same-origin session cookie (`sessionCookie`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`,
`SameSite=Strict`). Every state-changing request made with a session, including sign-in, must
carry the session's anti-forgery token in the `X-CSRF-Token` header (`csrfToken`), whatever
its content type. The flow is:

1. `GET /csrf-token` starts an anonymous session and returns its token. The token stays valid
   for the lifetime of the session, including across sign-in. A `403` with type
   `/api/v2/problems/csrf-token-mismatch` means the session ended: fetch a new token and retry
   once.
2. Sign in with a passkey (`POST /session/passkey-challenge`, then
   `POST /session/passkey-assertion`) or with a password (`POST /session`).
3. If the password step answers with state `pendingSecondFactor`, complete one of the listed
   methods (`POST /session/pending-sign-in/second-factor`, after
   `POST /session/pending-sign-in/webauthn-challenge` for WebAuthn) or cancel it
   (`DELETE /session/pending-sign-in`).
4. Sign out with `DELETE /session`.

**Automation clients** send an API key in the `X-API-Key` header (`apiKeyAuth`). A request
with a key never creates a session and needs no anti-forgery token. When a request carries
both a key and a session cookie, the key decides and the cookie is ignored. Any request that
carries a non-empty `X-API-Key` header is authenticated by that key, and an invalid, expired
or revoked key, or a key used from a disallowed address, is reported to mailcow's fail2ban.
The System operations (health checks, the contract, the documentation and the problem pages)
ignore `X-API-Key`.

## Recommended presentation of sign-in methods

Clients should offer **passkey sign-in first** whenever the device supports WebAuthn
(`PublicKeyCredential` is available), and username and password second. Passkeys registered
in the legacy UI under the names "FIDO2" or "Touch ID" are ordinary passkeys and need no
special handling. In the second-factor step, `PendingSignIn.methods` is already in the
recommended order: WebAuthn security keys and passkeys first, TOTP second, Yubico OTP last.
Methods with `tier: primary` are offered directly; methods with `tier: advanced` belong behind
an "other methods" option.

## Restricted sessions

When mailcow forces an account to change its password or to set up a second factor, the
session is restricted (`state: restricted`, non-empty `pendingActions`). It can read
`GET /me`, sign out and, when only `secondFactorSetup` is pending, register a passkey.
Operations that need no signed-in account stay available: `GET /csrf-token`, `GET /session`,
sign-in and its steps, the public configuration, the documentation and the health checks.
Every other operation answers `403` with type `/api/v2/problems/pending-action-required`.
API keys are never restricted: `Identity.pendingActions` is empty for them. Pending actions are re-evaluated from mailcow's
data on every request, so a restriction lifts as soon as it is resolved in either UI.

get.description:
Returns the anti-forgery token of the caller's session and starts an anonymous session (sets
the session cookie) when there is none. Call it once when the web app starts and after a
`csrf-token-mismatch` problem. The token stays valid until the session ends, including
across sign-in.

Returns the state of the caller's browser session: `anonymous`, `pendingSecondFactor` (with
the methods to offer), `restricted` (with the pending actions) or `active`. Never fails for a
missing or ended session; it reports `anonymous` instead. Requests with an API key are refused
with `session-required`.

post.summary: Sign in with username and password
post.description:
Verifies an existing mailcow username and password, for every role, with every password hash
format mailcow accepts. Signing in never modifies the stored hash.

- Without an active second factor the session becomes `active`, or `restricted` when mailcow
  forces a password change or second-factor setup. All of the account's second-factor entries
  are re-activated (legacy "disable second factor for the next login").
- With active second factors the session becomes `pendingSecondFactor` and lists the methods
  in the recommended order. Complete one within 5 minutes.
- A mailbox user's password verification records a recent-login entry (mailcow `sasl_log`),
  as legacy does.

Failures return one generic `sign-in-failed` error, are audited and are published to mailcow's
fail2ban channel as `mailcow UI: Invalid password for <username> by <client address>` (not for
mailboxes that authenticate against an external identity provider). Each failure for the same
username and client address is answered 0.5 s later than the previous one; after 10 failures
within 15 minutes attempts are refused with `429` without checking the password. A correct
password resets the count.

The session identifier is renewed when the step succeeds. A previous sign-in of the same
session is replaced.

delete.description:
Ends the session immediately in any state, including a pending sign-in, and audits the
sign-out of a signed-in account. Any further request with the old cookie is anonymous; fetch a
new anti-forgery token before signing in again. Without a live session the request succeeds
and changes nothing, and no anti-forgery token is needed.

Cancels a sign-in that awaits a second factor. The session returns to `anonymous` and keeps
its anti-forgery token. Succeeds and changes nothing when no sign-in is pending.

post.summary: Get a WebAuthn challenge for the pending sign-in
post.description:
Issues a single-use WebAuthn challenge, bound to the pending sign-in, that allows the
account's active WebAuthn second factors. It expires after 5 minutes or at the first
verification attempt. A new request replaces the previous challenge. User verification
follows mailcow's `WEBAUTHN_UV_FLAG_LOGIN`, and `extensions.appid` is set as in legacy.

post.summary: Complete the pending sign-in with a second factor
post.description:
Verifies one of the pending sign-in's methods: a TOTP code, a WebAuthn assertion or a Yubico
OTP. Second factors enrolled in the legacy UI verify without re-enrolment.

On success the session identifier is renewed, the session becomes `active` (or `restricted`)
and the sign-in is audited with `authMethod: passwordAndSecondFactor`.

One failed attempt cancels the pending sign-in (`second-factor-failed`), counts towards the
sign-in throttling of the username and client address, and is audited. A method that was
deactivated or deleted since the password step also cancels it. A TOTP code is accepted only
once within its validity window. When the Yubico service is unreachable the answer is `503`,
the pending sign-in stays open and nothing is counted. A malformed request (`422`) changes
nothing.

Issues a single-use challenge for usernameless passkey sign-in, bound to the session, with
an empty `allowCredentials` list so that the device offers its discoverable credentials for
this host. It expires after 5 minutes or at the first sign-in attempt. A new request replaces
the previous challenge. User verification follows mailcow's `FIDO2_UV_FLAG_LOGIN` (default
`preferred`).

Verifies an assertion for the session's passkey challenge and signs in the account that owns
the credential, with no password and no further second factor. Passkeys registered in the
legacy UI ("FIDO2", "Touch ID") work unchanged.

The credential must be active and its account must be able to sign in (active account, active
mailbox and domain, not a resource mailbox). Without `role`, the account type is resolved in
mailcow's order (administrator or domain administrator, then mailbox user); with `role`, an
account of another type fails. Forced password change and second-factor setup restrict the
session as after a password sign-in. A mailbox user's sign-in records a recent-login entry.

Failures return the generic `sign-in-failed` error, are audited and count towards throttling
per client address. They are not reported to fail2ban. The session identifier is renewed on
success.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated caller: username, role, how it authenticated, scope, effective
permission flags, pending actions and, for sessions, the preferences. For an API key it
returns the owner's role, scope and flags together with the key's identifier, name and access
level. Available in restricted sessions.
Returns the signed-in user's language and theme. Not available to API keys.

patch.description:
Changes the signed-in user's language (one of the enabled languages) and/or theme. The change
persists across sessions and devices and is audited. Not available to API keys.

get.description:
Lists the signed-in user's passkeys, including those registered in the legacy UI as "FIDO2"
or "Touch ID" credentials. `q` searches the name and the authenticator description. Not
available to API keys or in restricted sessions.

post.description:
Verifies the authenticator's response to the session's registration options and saves the
passkey where legacy mailcow stores FIDO2 credentials, bound to this host name, so that it
works for usernameless sign-in in both UIs. User verification and accepted attestation formats
follow mailcow's `FIDO2_UV_FLAG_REGISTER` and `FIDO2_FORMATS`. The registration is audited.

Needs a full session, or a session restricted only by `secondFactorSetup`, which the
registration lifts immediately. Not available to API keys or during a pending sign-in.

Issues single-use registration options bound to the session: a discoverable credential
(`residentKey: required`) for this host name, with the account's existing passkeys excluded.
They expire after 5 minutes or at the first registration attempt. A new request replaces the
previous options. Same access rules as `registerPasskey`.

delete.description:
Removes the passkey from mailcow, so it no longer signs in through either UI. Removing the
last passkey is allowed, as in legacy. Audited.

get.description:
Lists API keys, including revoked and expired ones. Administrators only: a signed-in
administrator or a key owned by an administrator. Secrets are never included. `q` searches
the name, the prefix and the owner's username.

parameters.name: ownerUsername
parameters.description: Only keys owned by this account (exact match).

post.description:
Creates a key owned by an existing administrator or domain administrator, with an access
level, an optional expiry in the future and optional allowed source networks. The response
contains the secret exactly once; only its SHA-256 hash is stored. Audited without the
secret.

Only a signed-in administrator may create keys. Requests authenticated by a key are refused
with `session-required`, so that a leaked key cannot mint replacements for itself.

get.description:
Lists the active administrators and active domain administrators that can own an API key
(mailcow's `admin` table with `active = 1`), for the owner field of the key form. Mailbox users
are never listed. Administrators only: a signed-in administrator or a key owned by an
administrator, read-only keys included.

Returns one key with its owner, access level, networks, expiry, creation, last use (accurate
to the minute), status and revocation. Administrators only, as for `listApiKeys`.

post.description:
Revokes the key. It is refused from the very next request, stays listed with its revocation
time and the revoking administrator, and cannot be restored. Audited. Revoking an already
revoked key succeeds and changes nothing; this check comes before `If-Match`, so a retried
revocation never answers `412`.

Only a signed-in administrator may revoke keys; requests authenticated by a key are refused
with `session-required`.

get.description:
Returns the branding, login page options and languages configured in mailcow's legacy UI.
No authentication is needed. Values are read from mailcow on every request, so a change saved
in the legacy UI is visible immediately; clients revalidate with `If-None-Match`.

Returns the logo uploaded in the legacy UI. `404` when none is uploaded for this variant; the
public configuration then points to the default logo instead.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: Version from `Logo.url`. With a matching version the response is cacheable for a year.

get.description:
Lists audit records, newest first by default. Administrators only: a signed-in administrator
or a key owned by an administrator. Records cannot be changed or deleted through the API and
are removed after the configured retention period (365 days by default). `q` searches the
actor username, the target name and the user agent.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only records at or after this time.

parameters.name: eventType
parameters.description: Only these event types. Repeat the parameter for several.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: Only records whose actor username (including attempted usernames) or API key ID equals this value.

parameters.name: clientAddress
parameters.description: Only records from this IPv4 or IPv6 address, or from within this prefix.

get.description: Answers `200` while the PHP runtime serves requests. Checks no dependency and ignores `X-API-Key`.

Checks the MariaDB connection, the mailcow schema version (`versions.db_schema` must be one
this release supports), the Redis connection and that this API's own migrations are applied.
Ignores `X-API-Key`.
Returns the bundled OpenAPI document of the running release. Ignores `X-API-Key`.
HTML page that renders `GET /openapi.yaml`. All assets are served by the API itself. Ignores `X-API-Key`.

Human-readable documentation of a problem type, so that every documented `type` URI
dereferences on each installation. Rendered from `docs/problems.md`. Ignores `X-API-Key`.

200.description: The documentation of this problem type.

sessionCookie.name: __Host-restv2_session
sessionCookie.description:
Same-origin browser session. The cookie is `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`,
`Path=/` and has no `Domain`. It expires after the server's idle session lifetime
(mailcow's `SESSION_LIFETIME`, 3 hours by default) and when the user agent changes.

csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfToken.description:
Anti-forgery token of the current session, obtained from `GET /csrf-token`. Required on
every state-changing request made with a session.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyAuth.description:
Secret of an API key created by an administrator. The key acts with its owner's role,
scope and permission flags, limited by its access level.

CsrfToken.description: Anti-forgery token of the current session.

token.description: Send this value in the `X-CSRF-Token` header of every state-changing request.

Problem.description:
RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`). `type` is the stable machine-readable
code: compare it as an exact string. `title` and `detail` are English and may be reworded.
Extension members may be added later without notice.

type.description:
Problem type. Either one of the documented types (see `KnownProblemType` and
`docs/problems.md`) or `about:blank`, in which case the status code identifies the problem.

title.description: Short English summary of the problem type.

status.description: HTTP status code of this occurrence.

detail.description: English explanation of this occurrence. Never contains secrets.

requestId.description:
Identifier of the request (the W3C trace ID), also written to the service log and to any
audit record of the request.

PendingAction.description:
Action an account must complete before the session is fully usable.

- `passwordChange`: mailcow forces a password change (`force_pw_update`). Until password change
  arrives in this API, the user changes the password in the legacy UI.
- `secondFactorSetup`: mailcow forces second-factor setup (`force_tfa`) and the account has no
  second factor and no active passkey. Registering a passkey (`POST /me/passkeys`) resolves it.

PendingActionProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/pending-action-required` (status `403`). The session is
restricted until the listed actions are completed.

SessionState.description:
- `anonymous`: no account is signed in. The session only carries the anti-forgery token and
  any passkey challenge.
- `pendingSecondFactor`: the password was verified and one of `pendingSignIn.methods` must be
  completed within 5 minutes.
- `restricted`: signed in, but `pendingActions` must be completed first.
- `active`: signed in with full access for the account's role.

Role.description:
Account role. `admin` and `domainAdmin` accounts live in mailcow's `admin` table (`superadmin`
1 or 0); `mailboxUser` accounts are rows of the `mailbox` table.

SecondFactorType.description:
Second-factor type. `webauthn` covers security keys and passkeys enrolled as a second factor
(mailcow `tfa.authmech = webauthn`), `totp` authenticator apps, `yubiOtp` Yubico OTP keys
verified against the Yubico service. Deprecated U2F and HOTP entries are never offered.

SecondFactorMethod.description: One enrolled second factor. Never contains secret material.

tier.description:
`primary` for `webauthn` and `totp`, offered directly. `advanced` for `yubiOtp`, offered
behind an "other methods" option.

PendingSignIn.description:
A sign-in whose password was verified and which needs one second factor. `methods` lists the
account's active, usable second factors in the recommended presentation order: WebAuthn
security keys and passkeys first, TOTP second, Yubico OTP last. One failed attempt cancels the
pending sign-in.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes after the password step.

Session.description:
The browser session of the caller. `username` and `role` are present in every state except
`anonymous`. `authMethod` and `signedInAt` are present in `restricted` and `active`.
`pendingSignIn` is present only in `pendingSecondFactor`.

username.description: Normalised (trimmed, lower-cased) username of the account.

authMethod.description: How this session was signed in.

idleTimeout.description:
Seconds of inactivity after which the session ends (mailcow's `SESSION_LIFETIME`, 10800 by
default). Every request resets the timer.

PasswordSignInRequest.description:
Username and password of an existing mailcow account. The username is trimmed and lower-cased
before lookup. Without `role`, account types are tried in mailcow's order: administrator,
domain administrator, mailbox user. With `role`, only that type is tried.

ValidationRuleCode.description:
Stable code of a validation rule. Clients must treat unknown codes as a generic invalid value,
because later features may add codes.

- `required`: the field is missing, `null` or empty.
- `invalidType`: wrong JSON type. Params: `expected` (`string`, `integer`, `boolean`, `array`,
  `object`).
- `tooShort` / `tooLong`: string length out of bounds. Params: `min` / `max`.
- `tooMany`: too many list items. Params: `max`.
- `outOfRange`: number out of bounds. Params: `min`, `max`.
- `notInList`: value not among the allowed values. Params: `allowed`.
- `invalidFormat`: value does not match a format. Params: `format`, one of `dateTime`
  (RFC 3339), `ipNetwork` (IPv4 or IPv6 address or prefix), `ipAddress`, `totpCode` (six
  digits), `yubicoOtp` (44 letters or digits), `base64url`, `webauthnCredential`.
- `mustBeInFuture`: a time that must lie in the future does not.
- `notFound`: the referenced object does not exist.
- `notEligible`: the referenced object exists but cannot be used here. Params: `allowedRoles`.

FieldViolation.description: One violated validation rule of one field.

params.description:
Parameters of the rule, for building a translated message. Known keys: `min`, `max`
(numbers), `allowed` (list of allowed values), `format` (name of the expected format, see
`ValidationRuleCode`), `expected` (expected JSON type) and `allowedRoles`.

message.description: English message for logs and scripts. Clients translate from `code` and `params`.

ValidationProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/validation-failed` (status `422`). `errors` maps each invalid
field to its violations. Body fields use their dot-separated path in the request body
(`allowedNetworks.2`); query parameters use their name (`limit`); the key `body` stands for the
request body as a whole (for example an empty merge patch).

language.message: The selected language is not enabled on this server.

TooManyRequestsProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/too-many-requests` (status `429`). The `Retry-After` header
carries the same value as `retryAfter`.

retryAfter.description: Seconds until the next attempt will be considered.

Base64Url.description: Unpadded base64url encoding (RFC 4648, section 5) of binary data.

WebAuthnRequestOptions.description:
`PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON` of WebAuthn Level 3. Pass it to
`PublicKeyCredential.parseRequestOptionsFromJSON()` and then to `navigator.credentials.get()`.

rpId.description: Host name serving the API and the web app.

allowCredentials.description: Empty for passkey sign-in (discoverable credentials); the account's WebAuthn second factors otherwise.

extensions.description: Client extension inputs. The second-factor challenge sets `appid` as legacy mailcow does.

WebAuthnChallenge.description: A single-use WebAuthn challenge bound to the session.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes after issue. The challenge is consumed by the first verification attempt.

TotpSecondFactor.description:
A code from the authenticator app enrolled as method `methodId`. A code accepted once is not
accepted again within its validity window.

methodId.description: `id` of a `totp` method of the pending sign-in.

WebAuthnAuthenticationResponse.description:
`AuthenticationResponseJSON` of WebAuthn Level 3, as returned by
`PublicKeyCredential.prototype.toJSON()` after `navigator.credentials.get()`.

WebAuthnSecondFactor.description:
Assertion for the challenge from `POST /session/pending-sign-in/webauthn-challenge`. The
credential must be one of the pending sign-in's `webauthn` methods.

YubiOtpSecondFactor.description:
A Yubico OTP. The key is identified by the OTP's public ID among the account's active Yubico OTP
methods and verified against the Yubico service with the credentials stored in mailcow.

SecondFactorVerification.description: Proof for one of the pending sign-in's methods.

PasskeySignInRequest.description:
Assertion for the challenge from `POST /session/passkey-challenge`. The account is the owner of
the credential. With `role`, the sign-in fails unless that account is of that role.

AuthMethod.description:
How the caller authenticated: `password` (no second factor active), `passwordAndSecondFactor`,
`passkey` (usernameless passkey sign-in) or `apiKey`.

ApiKeyAccessLevel.description: `readOnly` keys may only call safe methods (GET, HEAD); `readWrite` keys may also change state.

IdentityAuthentication.description: How the caller authenticated. `apiKey` is present only when `method` is `apiKey`.

prefix.description: Non-secret leading characters of the key.

Scope.description:
Objects the caller may reach: every domain for an administrator, the managed domains for a
domain administrator (active assignments in mailcow's `domain_admins`), the own mailbox for a
mailbox user. A domain administrator without domains has an empty list.

PermissionFlags.description:
Effective permission flags, named after the columns of mailcow's `user_acl` and `da_acl` tables
in camelCase. An administrator has every flag. A domain administrator has every `user_acl` flag,
overridden by its own `da_acl` row where the names overlap (`syncjobs`, `quarantine`,
`appPasswds`, `pushover`, `spamPolicy`). A mailbox user has its `user_acl` row and `false` for
the flags that exist only in `da_acl`. This is the legacy `acl('to_session')` logic.

Preferences.description:
Per-account web app preferences, stored by this API and shared by every device. Defaults: the
server's default language and `system`. A stored language that is no longer enabled falls back
to the default language.

language.description: One of the enabled language codes from `GET /public-config`.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored settings, equal to the `ETag` header of a single read. Send it in
`If-Match` when changing the resource.

Identity.description:
The authenticated caller. Role, scope, permission flags, account status and pending actions are
evaluated from mailcow's current data on every request, so changes made in either UI apply to
the next request. For an API key, `username` and `role` are those of the key's owner.

pendingActions.description: Pending actions of a session. Always empty for an API key, which is never restricted.

PreferencesPatch.description: JSON Merge Patch of `Preferences`. Omitted members stay unchanged.

language.description: Must be one of the enabled language codes.

Passkey.description:
A passkey of the signed-in account: a discoverable WebAuthn credential stored where legacy
mailcow stores FIDO2 credentials (table `fido2`), so it works in both UIs.

id.description: Non-secret identifier, the SHA-256 of the credential ID in hex (the legacy `cid`).

name.description: Display name chosen by the user (`fido2.friendlyName`), `null` when never set.

authenticatorDescription.description:
Subject of the attestation certificate (`fido2.certificateSubject`), `null` when the
authenticator sent none. Legacy shows "Unknown" with the registration date in that case.

hostName.description: Host name the passkey is bound to (`fido2.rpId`). It only works on that host.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored settings, equal to the `ETag` header of a single read. Send it in
`If-Match` when changing the resource.

ListMeta.description: Pagination metadata of a list response.

total.description: Number of items matching the filters, ignoring `limit` and `offset`.

WebAuthnRegistrationResponse.description:
`RegistrationResponseJSON` of WebAuthn Level 3, as returned by
`PublicKeyCredential.prototype.toJSON()` after `navigator.credentials.create()`.

PasskeyRegistrationRequest.description: Authenticator response to the options from `POST /me/passkeys/registration-options`.

name.description: Optional display name. It can be set or changed later with `PATCH`.

WebAuthnCreationOptions.description:
`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` of WebAuthn Level 3. Pass it to
`PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON()` and then to `navigator.credentials.create()`.

alg.description: COSE algorithm identifier (for example -7 for ES256, -257 for RS256).

excludeCredentials.description: Passkeys already registered to the account, so the authenticator refuses duplicates.

PasskeyRegistrationOptions.description: Single-use passkey registration options bound to the session.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes after issue. The options are consumed by the first registration attempt.

PasskeyPatch.description: JSON Merge Patch of a passkey. Only the display name can change.

ApiKeyStatus.description:
`revoked` once revoked (final), otherwise `expired` once `expiresAt` has passed, otherwise
`active`. A key whose owner is inactive or deleted keeps its status but is rejected as invalid
(see `owner.active`).

ApiKeyOwner.description:
The account whose role, scope and permission flags the key acts with, evaluated on every
request. `role` is `null` when the account no longer exists.

active.description: `false` when the owner is deactivated or deleted. The key is then rejected as invalid.

AccountRef.description: Reference to a mailcow account by username.

ApiKey.description: An API key. The secret is never returned after creation.

prefix.description: Non-secret leading characters of the secret, for recognising the key.

allowedNetworks.description: Normalised IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes. Empty means any address.

lastUsedAt.description: Accurate to the minute. `null` when never used.

lastUsedFrom.description: Client address of the last use.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored settings (not of `lastUsedAt`, `lastUsedFrom` or `status`), equal to the `ETag` header of a single read. Send it in
`If-Match` when changing the resource.

ApiKeyCreateRequest.description:
A new API key. Keys cannot be edited: to change the access level, networks or expiry, create a
new key and revoke the old one.

ownerUsername.description: An existing administrator or domain administrator. Mailbox users cannot own keys.

expiresAt.description: Must be in the future. Omit or send `null` for a key that never expires.

allowedNetworks.description: IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or prefixes. Omit or send an empty list to allow any address.

ApiKeyCreated.description: A newly created API key with its secret. The secret is shown only in this response.

secret.description: Send it in the `X-API-Key` header. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored.

ApiKeyOwnerCandidate.description: An active administrator or domain administrator that can own an API key.

Logo.description:
A logo. When the operator uploaded one, `url` points to `GET /public-config/logos/{variant}`
with a version parameter that changes with the image. Otherwise `url` is the default logo of
the deployed legacy UI (`/img/cow_mailcow.svg` upstream), served by the legacy web root.

Announcement.description: Announcement banner (`UI_ANNOUNCEMENT_*`). The text is plain text.

active.description: Show the banner only when `active` is `true` and `text` is not `null`.

LoginPageOptions.description: Login page options (`CUSTOM_LOGIN`). All default to `false`.

hideDomainAdminLogin.description: Hide the domain administrator login link (`hide_domainadmin_quicklink`).

hideMailboxUserLogin.description: Hide the mailbox user login link (`hide_user_quicklink`).

forceSingleSignOn.description: Legacy hides the password form in favour of identity-provider sign-in (`force_sso`).

name.description: Native name as configured in mailcow.

AppLink.description:
A link of the apps menu. Built-in apps (`source: builtIn`) come from mailcow's `$MAILCOW_APPS`
(by default Webmail at `/SOGo/so`). Operator links (`source: operator`) come from the legacy
customisation "App links" (Redis `APP_LINKS`). Addresses are as configured: relative to the
mailcow host or absolute.

url.description: Address used on the login page (legacy `link`).

signedInUrl.description:
Address used for signed-in users (legacy `user_link`, or `link` when unset). It may contain
the placeholder `%u`, which the client replaces with the signed-in username, as legacy does.

description.description: Tooltip text of a built-in app (`$MAILCOW_APPS` `description`), `null` otherwise.

showOnLoginPage.description:
`false` when the link is hidden (legacy `hide`). Hiding applies only to the login page; the
apps menu of signed-in users shows every link.

PublicConfig.description:
Branding and login page settings for signed-out clients. Values come from mailcow's existing
customisation (the legacy admin UI's "Customize" screen) and language settings, so the
operator configures them in one place. Unset values fall back to the defaults the deployed
legacy UI shows. Contains no secrets and nothing account-specific.

`loginHelpHtml` and `footerHtml` contain operator-authored HTML, rendered unescaped by the
legacy UI. Clients must sanitise them before rendering. Every other text is plain text.

productName.description: Name shown on the login page (`MAIN_NAME`). Same default as `pageTitle`.

loginHelpHtml.description: Operator HTML shown below the login form (`HELP_TEXT`), `null` when unset.

configured.description:
`true` when mailcow has an external identity provider (Keycloak, generic OIDC or LDAP)
configured. Sign-in through it is not available in this API yet.

appsLabel.description:
Label of the apps menu set by the operator (`APPS_NAME`, plain text). `null` when unset; the
client then shows its own translated "Apps".

appLinks.description:
App links in legacy order: built-in apps first, then operator links in their stored order.
Built-in apps that point to SOGo are left out when SOGo is disabled (`SKIP_SOGO=y`). Show the
login-page block only when at least one link has `showOnLoginPage: true`.

AuditEventType.description: Audited event. Later features add values; clients must tolerate unknown ones.

AuditActor.description:
Who acted. For a failed sign-in, `username` is the attempted username when one is known and
`role` may be `null`. `apiKeyId` is set when the request was authenticated by an API key.

AuditFailureReason.description:
Why an audited operation failed. Later features add values.

- `invalidCredentials`: unknown account, wrong password or malformed username.
- `accountInactive`: inactive account, inactive domain or resource mailbox.
- `externalIdentitySource`: the mailbox authenticates against LDAP or an OIDC provider.
- `unknownPasskey`, `passkeyInactive`, `roleMismatch`, `passkeyVerificationFailed`.
- `challengeExpired`: pending sign-in, challenge or registration options missing, used or expired.
- `secondFactorFailed`, `secondFactorUnavailable`, `verificationUnavailable` (Yubico service).
- `throttled`: refused by sign-in throttling without checking credentials.
- `registrationFailed`: the authenticator's registration response was rejected.

AuditEvent.description:
One immutable audit record. Never contains passwords, one-time codes, WebAuthn assertions, key
secrets or session identifiers.

clientAddress.description: Real client address as seen by mailcow's reverse proxy.

details.description:
Non-secret event details, for example `requestedRole`, `secondFactorType`,
`changedFields` or `accessLevel`.

HealthCheckStatus.description:
`ok`, or `failed`. For `schema`, `failed` means the mailcow database schema version
(`versions.db_schema`) is not one this release supports.

ReadinessProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/service-unavailable` (status `503`) returned by the readiness
check, with the result of each dependency check.

Unauthorized.description:
The caller is not authenticated. Possible types:
- `/api/v2/problems/unauthenticated`: no session and no API key, or the session ended (idle
  timeout, sign-out, changed user agent, account deactivated or deleted).
- `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-required`: the session's sign-in still awaits a second factor.
- `/api/v2/problems/api-key-invalid`: the key matches no key, or its owner is inactive or deleted.
- `/api/v2/problems/api-key-expired`, `/api/v2/problems/api-key-revoked`.

value.title: Authentication required
value.detail: Sign in or send a valid API key.

value.title: API key revoked
value.detail: The API key was revoked and can no longer be used.

Forbidden.description:
The caller is authenticated but may not perform this request. Possible types:
- `/api/v2/problems/forbidden`: the caller's role or permission flags do not allow it.
- `/api/v2/problems/csrf-token-mismatch`: a session request without a valid `X-CSRF-Token`.
- `/api/v2/problems/session-required`: the operation is not available to API keys.
- `/api/v2/problems/pending-action-required`: the session is restricted (extension `pendingActions`).
- `/api/v2/problems/insufficient-key-scope`: a read-only key used for a state-changing request.
- `/api/v2/problems/api-key-source-not-allowed`: the key is used from an address outside its
  allowed networks.

value.title: Pending action required
value.detail: Complete the pending actions before using this operation.

InternalError.description: Unexpected failure (type `about:blank`). Nothing was changed, and no audit record was lost.

SessionCreated.description: Sign-in step succeeded. The session identifier was renewed. `state` is `active`, `restricted` or `pendingSecondFactor`.

Location.description: Absolute path of the created resource.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request, for example a body that is not valid JSON (type `about:blank`).

SignInRejected.description:
The sign-in step failed. Possible types:
- `/api/v2/problems/sign-in-failed`: one generic error for an unknown account, a wrong password,
  an inactive account or domain, a resource mailbox, a malformed username, a mailbox that
  authenticates against an external identity provider, and an unknown, inactive or
  wrong-role passkey. It never reveals which.
- `/api/v2/problems/sign-in-expired`: there is no pending sign-in or challenge in this session,
  or it expired or was already used. Start again.
- `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-failed`: the second factor was wrong or no longer exists. The
  pending sign-in is cancelled; start again with the password.
- The API key types of `Unauthorized` when the request carries an invalid `X-API-Key`.

value.title: Sign-in failed
value.detail: The credentials are invalid or the account cannot sign in.

SignInForbidden.description:
The sign-in request is refused. Possible types:
- `/api/v2/problems/csrf-token-mismatch`: missing or wrong `X-CSRF-Token`. Call
  `GET /csrf-token` first.
- `/api/v2/problems/session-required`: the request carries an API key; sign-in is for browser
  sessions only.
- `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-unavailable`: the password is correct, but the account's only
  active second factors are deprecated U2F or HOTP entries. An administrator must reset them.
- `/api/v2/problems/insufficient-key-scope` and `/api/v2/problems/api-key-source-not-allowed`:
  the request carries a read-only API key, or a key used from a disallowed address.

TooManyRequests.description:
Throttled (type `/api/v2/problems/too-many-requests`). Sign-in attempts are refused after 10
failures for the same username and client address (passkeys: the same client address) within
15 minutes, without checking credentials.

Retry-After.description: Seconds after which the request may be retried.

WebAuthnChallengeResponse.description: A single-use WebAuthn challenge bound to the session.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state of the resource (type `about:blank`). See `detail`.

TemporaryVerificationFailure.description:
The Yubico verification service could not be reached (type
`/api/v2/problems/temporary-verification-failure`). The pending sign-in stays open, so another
method can be tried, and the attempt does not count towards throttling.

Retry-After.description: Seconds after which the request may be retried.

ETag.description: Version tag (strong ETag) of the resource's stored settings, equal to `data.etag`. Send it in `If-Match` when changing the resource.

PreconditionFailed.description: The `If-Match` header does not match the current representation (type `about:blank`). Nothing changed.

Location.description: Absolute path of the created resource.

ETag.description: Version tag (strong ETag) of the resource's stored settings, equal to `data.etag`. Send it in `If-Match` when changing the resource.

PasskeyRegistrationRejected.description:
The registration was rejected. Possible types:
- `/api/v2/problems/passkey-registration-failed`: the registration options are missing, used
  or expired, the authenticator response does not verify (challenge, origin, host name, user
  verification, attestation format), or the credential is already registered.
- `about:blank`: the body is not valid JSON.

PasskeyRegistrationOptionsResponse.description: Single-use registration options bound to the session.

ETag.description: Version tag (strong ETag) of the resource's stored settings, equal to `data.etag`. Send it in `If-Match` when changing the resource.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist or is outside the caller's scope (type `about:blank`).

ApiKeyCreatedResponse.description: The key was created. This is the only response that contains the secret.

Location.description: Absolute path of the created resource.

ETag.description: Version tag (strong ETag) of the resource's stored settings, equal to `data.etag`. Send it in `If-Match` when changing the resource.

ApiKeyOwnerCandidateListResponse.description: Accounts that can own an API key.

ETag.description: Version tag (strong ETag) of the resource's stored settings, equal to `data.etag`. Send it in `If-Match` when changing the resource.

PublicConfigResponse.description: The public configuration. Changes saved in the legacy UI are visible on the next request.

ETag.description: Strong entity tag of the representation. Send it in `If-None-Match` to revalidate.

NotModified.description: The representation matching `If-None-Match` is still current.

ETag.description: Strong entity tag of the current representation.

LogoImage.description:
The logo image uploaded in the legacy UI, with the media type it was uploaded with (GIF, JPEG,
PNG or SVG). Responses with the `v` query parameter are cacheable for a year.

ETag.description: Strong entity tag of the image.

Cache-Control.description: `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` with a matching `v`, `no-cache` otherwise.

Content-Security-Policy.description: `default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; sandbox`, so that SVG logos cannot run scripts.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Not ready (type `/api/v2/problems/service-unavailable`), with the failed checks.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description:
`ETag` from a previous read, or `*`. When it does not match the current representation, the
request fails with `412` and nothing changes.

Order.name: order
Order.description: Sort direction. Each list documents its default.

Search.name: q
Search.description:
Case-insensitive substring search over the list's documented search fields. Leading and trailing
whitespace is ignored; an empty value means no search.

PasskeyId.name: passkeyId
PasskeyId.description: `id` of one of the caller's passkeys. Other accounts' passkeys answer `404`.

ProblemTypeName.name: problemType
ProblemTypeName.description: Last path segment of a documented problem type URI.
